title.en: Introduction to Harappan Seals and Images
title.hi: हड़प्पा की मुहरें और छवियां: परिचय

content.en: The study of **Harappan seals and images** provides invaluable insights into the material culture, religious beliefs, administrative mechanisms, and artistic achievements of the **Indus Valley Civilisation**. Among the most prolific and sophisticated artifacts recovered from Harappan sites, these objects demonstrate an exceptional standard of miniature carving and metallurgical skill. **Steatite** is the most common material used for crafting seals, though examples made of terracotta, agate, chert, copper, and faience are also discovered. These small, portable objects served multifaceted purposes, acting simultaneously as markers of economic authority, amulets of social identity, and windows into the cosmological worldview of the civilization.
content.hi: **हड़प्पा की मुहरों और छवियों (Harappan seals and images)** का अध्ययन **सिंधु घाटी सभ्यता (Indus Valley Civilisation)** की भौतिक संस्कृति, धार्मिक मान्यताओं, प्रशासनिक तंत्र और कलात्मक उपलब्धियों के बारे में अमूल्य जानकारी प्रदान करता है। हड़प्पा स्थलों से प्राप्त सबसे प्रचुर और परिष्कृत कलाकृतियों में से एक, ये वस्तुएं लघुचित्र नक्काशी और धातुकर्म कौशल के एक असाधारण मानक को प्रदर्शित करती हैं। **खड़िया पत्थर (Steatite)** मुहरें बनाने के लिए सबसे आम सामग्री है, हालांकि टेराकोटा, अगेट (गोमेद), चर्ट, तांबा और फ़ैयेंस से बनी वस्तुएं भी पाई जाती हैं। ये छोटी, पोर्टेबल वस्तुएं बहुआयामी उद्देश्यों को पूरा करती थीं, जो एक साथ आर्थिक अधिकार के प्रतीकों, सामाजिक पहचान के ताबीज और सभ्यता के ब्रह्मांड संबंधी विश्वदृष्टि में खिड़की के रूप में कार्य करती थीं।

definition.en: The majority of seals were carved from **steatite** (a soft magnesian rock), then coated with an alkali and heated to produce a glossy, white surface finish. Intaglio engraving was executed using micro-chisels and fine drills.
definition.hi: The majority of seals were carved from **steatite** (a soft magnesian rock), then coated with an alkali and heated to produce a glossy, white surface finish. Intaglio engraving was executed using micro-chisels and fine drills.

definition.en: Most seals feature a line of **undeciphered pictographic script** across the top, generally written from right to left in the bougrophedon style on longer lines, serving as owner identification or administrative legends.
definition.hi: Most seals feature a line of **undeciphered pictographic script** across the top, generally written from right to left in the bougrophedon style on longer lines, serving as owner identification or administrative legends.

definition.en: Faunal representations are remarkably realistic, featuring the unicorn, humped bull (zebu), elephant, tiger, rhinoceros, bison, and composite animals reflecting high acute observation by Harappan artisans.
definition.hi: Faunal representations are remarkably realistic, featuring the unicorn, humped bull (zebu), elephant, tiger, rhinoceros, bison, and composite animals reflecting high acute observation by Harappan artisans.

definition.en: A small boss with a perforated hole is typically present on the reverse side of square seals, indicating they were likely worn as amulets or used as pendants by merchants and elites.
definition.hi: A small boss with a perforated hole is typically present on the reverse side of square seals, indicating they were likely worn as amulets or used as pendants by merchants and elites.

content.en: Discovered at Mohenjo-daro, this seal depicts a three-headed male deity seated in a yogic posture (mulabandhasana) on a low throne. Surrounded by wild animals and bearing proto-Shiva iconographic elements, it highlights early traditions of asceticism, yoga, and animal lordship in South Asian religion.
content.hi: Discovered at Mohenjo-daro, this seal depicts a three-headed male deity seated in a yogic posture (mulabandhasana) on a low throne. Surrounded by wild animals and bearing proto-Shiva iconographic elements, it highlights early traditions of asceticism, yoga, and animal lordship in South Asian religion.

content.en: Harappan metalworkers mastered the **cire-perdue** (lost-wax) method for crafting metallic figurines. The 'Dancing Girl' from Mohenjo-daro is an exceptional example, showcasing dynamic posture, sophisticated metallurgy, and a complete lack of monumental stone statuary in favor of exquisite miniature art.
content.hi: Harappan metalworkers mastered the **cire-perdue** (lost-wax) method for crafting metallic figurines. The 'Dancing Girl' from Mohenjo-daro is an exceptional example, showcasing dynamic posture, sophisticated metallurgy, and a complete lack of monumental stone statuary in favor of exquisite लघुचित्र art.

content.en: Unlike the elite steatite seals and bronze sculptures, **terracotta figurines** are found in abundance across domestic contexts. They include mother goddess figures, wheeled toy animals, carts, and masked heads, pointing towards popular folk religion and domestic amusement.
content.hi: Unlike the elite steatite seals and bronze sculptures, **terracotta figurines** are found in abundance across domestic contexts. They include mother goddess figures, wheeled toy animals, carts, and masked heads, pointing towards popular folk religion and domestic amusement.

content.en: Seals were primarily administrative tools pressed onto damp clay lump sealings attached to merchandise bundles, rope knots, and storage jars. They functioned as tamper-proof security tokens that facilitated long-distance mercantile exchange across Mesopotamia and the Indus basin.
content.hi: Seals were primarily administrative tools pressed onto damp clay lump sealings attached to merchandise bundles, rope knots, and storage jars. They functioned as tamper-proof security tokens that facilitated long-distance mercantile exchange across Mesopotamia and the Indus basin.

content.en: Students often assume seals were exclusively used as currency or coins. They were actually administrative tokens, commercial stamps, and amulets, not a monetary currency.
content.hi: Students often assume seals were exclusively used as currency or coins. They were actually administrative tokens, commercial stamps, and amulets, not a monetary currency.

content.en: In Mains GS-1, connect the naturalistic style of Harappan art (like the stone torso or bronze dancer) to the advanced urban planning and technological specialization of the civilization.
content.hi: In Mains GS-1, connect the naturalistic style of Harappan art (like the stone torso or bronze dancer) to the advanced urban planning and technological specialization of the civilization.

content.en: The most common motif found on Harappan seals is the 'Unicorn' (a single-horned mythical beast shown in profile with a ritual stand), outnumbering even the humped zebu bull.
content.hi: The most common motif found on Harappan seals is the 'Unicorn' (a single-horned mythical beast shown in profile with a ritual stand), outnumbering even the humped zebu bull.

keyTakeaways.en: Steatite was the preferred medium for carving miniature intaglio seals, finished with an alkaline glaze.
keyTakeaways.hi: Steatite was the preferred medium for carving लघुचित्र intaglio seals, finished with an alkaline glaze.

keyTakeaways.en: The Pashupati seal from Mohenjo-daro offers crucial evidence for early yogic traditions and proto-historic religion.
keyTakeaways.hi: The Pashupati seal from Mohenjo-daro offers crucial evidence for early yogic traditions and proto-historic religion.

keyTakeaways.en: Metal sculptures like the Dancing Girl demonstrate advanced mastery of the lost-wax (cire-perdue) casting technique.
keyTakeaways.hi: Metal sculptures like the Dancing Girl demonstrate advanced mastery of the lost-wax (cire-perdue) casting technique.

keyTakeaways.en: Seals functioned primarily as administrative security markers and elite identity tokens rather than currency.
